habitat: Singly or in small parties, often with Three-banded Plover, on shorelines of coastal lagoons, estuaries and inland waters.
summary: An uncommon summer visitor. A dumpy, short-billed plover. The orange-yellow legs and the single bold black breast-band around the neck are diagnostic. The male has a black mask. In flight it shows a white wing-bar, unlike the Three-banded Plover. The call is coo-eep or too-li.

similar.note: Three-banded Plover has two black breast-bands, a red bill and a red eye-ring, and no white wing-bar. Ringed Plover has one black band, orange-yellow legs and a white wing-bar.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^5=32 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 16–64.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

calls.description: coo-eep or too-li. The texts do not separate the sexes. Grade A from Degernäs, Sweden. The filename uses the Swedish name Större strandpipare. A South African file was grade C.

research.note: Status is a Palearctic migrant. Newman calls it an uncommon summer visitor and does not name the months, so monthsPresent was left unset. The female is not separated. The call is grade A from Sweden. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.
